Ai._comment_Tier: MODEL-TIER SURFACE POLICY IN PRODUCTION (tier-ux-rework plan, c2). ConsentRequired is FALSE here and it is written out EXPLICITLY rather than left to inherit: an object block in this file REPLACES the base appsettings.json block at the key level rather than merging into it, so an omitted key does not inherit the base file's true - it falls through to AiTierOptions.ConsentRequired's class default (also true), which would silently re-enable the step in prod. WHY FALSE: consent exists to tell an author that an unpublished manuscript is about to leave the machine, and in a hosted deployment BOTH tiers already run off-machine, so the step would ask for consent to something that already happened on the fast tier. A confirm dialog that is always wrong is worse than none - it teaches people to click through the ones that matter. This is the DEPLOYMENT'S TOPOLOGY talking, not a product opinion, which is why it is config and not a constant. IT REMOVES NO ENFORCEMENT: the 409 on a 'thinking' request this deployment cannot route is unconditional and independent of this flag. KEEP IN SYNC with base appsettings.json (true there) - AiTierConsentFlagConfigParityTests binds both files and fails if either value moves.

Ai._comment_AnalysisRepair: Production policy for the analysis-output repair layer (Ai:AnalysisRepair, see AnalysisRepairOptions in Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs). This block MIRRORS base appsettings.json (Enabled:true, GuardOnly:true, Mode:GlossaryThenDynamic, glossary-on for all PerType) because prod currently serves Ollama-LOCAL models via Ai:FeatureModels (gemma4:12b / qwen3.5:9b / DictaLM-3.0) - a leaky tier where the deterministic glossary guard still earns its keep. KEEP IN SYNC with Ai:FeatureModels: the model actually served in prod. Do NOT make this a no-op on the assumption a cloud tier is leak-free: a 2026-07-10 3-passage cloud sweep (google/gemma-4-31b-it via OpenRouter) leaked English into Hebrew prose at the SAME ~1/3 rate as local gemma4:12b (local leaked 'confusion', cloud leaked 'claustrophobia'; both out-of-glossary abstract nouns). No measured tier is leak-free on this task, so keep the guard ON across tiers (it is a zero-cost no-op on clean fields). CAVEAT: the deterministic glossary only cleans its 23 curated craft terms (LiteraryTermGlossary.Terms), NOT the general-vocabulary leaks seen in the wild - a dynamic detect-and-repair replacement for the closed glossary (DynamicTermRepairService, dynamic-term-repair-design plan) EXISTS and is turned ON in prod via Mode=GlossaryThenDynamic (the span-scoped dynamic stage runs AFTER the glossary fast-path; flip Mode back to Glossary/Off to disable it, and Enabled=false remains the master off-switch). The ON default rests on the 2026-07-12 RE-MEASURE (be-c08, docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 18), which drove the REAL BookEntityProvider over a real DbContext on the shipped LOCAL gemma4:12b tier: out-of-glossary cleaning 100% (10/10), unchanged (delta 0 percentage points, 0 leaks spared) when an adversarial per-book entity set is active; legitimate-term preservation 100% (21/21) with 0 false positives; over-rewrite 0; and 0 legitimate values reaching the model, so precision here is a property of the DETERMINISTIC GATE rather than of the model tier. It SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-11 d5/d6 tables (section 17), which fed a hand-built entity set and therefore never exercised the harvest logic or the bookId threading that actually ship. KEEP THIS BLOCK IN SYNC with base appsettings.json: AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.Mode_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual fails if the two Mode values diverge. Extension point (documented only, NOT implemented): a per-provider/per-model override on AnalysisRepairOptions is only needed if a single environment ever serves MULTIPLE tiers at once (e.g. some requests to a cloud model, others to local Ollama, in the same deployment) - see the AnalysisRepairOptions xmldoc in Services/Ai/AiOptions.cs for the full note. SummaryBatchWindowChapters (be-c03) also mirrors base appsettings.json - see its _comment_SummaryBatchWindowChapters for the full rationale; it bounds how many chapters the chapter-summary pass summarizes and repairs before committing, so an abort cannot discard a whole 80-chapter book's work. AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.SummaryBatchWindowChapters_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual fails if the two values diverge.

AnalysisRepair._comment_PerTypeExclusions: h3 (analysis-repair-pertype-coverage-holes plan, 2026-07-28) makes the per-type decisions EXPLICIT rather than merely absent, so each one is visible at the config surface instead of inferred from a missing line. An explicit false is semantically IDENTICAL to absence under AnalysisRepairGate.Evaluate (present-and-false and absent both return PerTypeExcluded). Custom: DELIBERATELY false (d1, reasoning NARROWED by c1) - its instruction is user-authored (req.CustomPrompt), so the output is legitimately English / bilingual / quoted / tabular, which falsifies the layer's foreign-script=leak premise; and repair cost is one model call per foreign WORD with no cap, so an English answer would be both mistranslated and a several-hundred-call GPU wedge. c1 then MEASURED the real corpus (analysis-repair-coverage-followups plan, 2026-07-28): n=16 rows / 6 distinct instructions / 1 user / 2 books, Hebrew script fraction 1.0000 on EVERY row, max offline REPAIR-classified run count 0, rows with at least one repair run 0/16 (Wilson 95% CI 0.0-19.4%) - so an enabled Custom repair would clean NOTHING on the real data while the uncapped cost stays merely unsampled, and the pick-frequency assumption remains un-measured. Note the exclusion does not rest on this key alone: Custom has NO dispatch arm in ANY of the THREE per-type dispatch switches (GlossaryRepairPass.Apply, DynamicTermRepairService.ApplyAsync, AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync), so flipping this key to true today would change nothing at all - enabling it means adding three dispatch arms first. See the plan's '## d1 decision' and '## c1 findings'. Synopsis: WAS deliberately false (q1: 83% preservation, 1 false positive) and is now TRUE (f2, 2026-07-28). q2 RE-MEASURED it on q1's OWN fixtures after ForeignRunClassifier rule (7b) landed, and the section-18.2 bar CLEARED: preservation 100% (6/6), false positives 0, over-rewrite 0, cleaning 100% (3/3), on the shipped LOCAL tier (Ollama | gemma4:12b) and reproduced identically on cloud gemma-4-31b-it. READ THAT 100% CORRECTLY: 0 of the 6 legitimate values reach the model, so it is a property of the DETERMINISTIC GATE (1 entity-gated, 5 classifier-rule-gated, 0 model) and not of gemma4:12b - rule (7b) does not make the model better at proper nouns, it stops asking it. THE GPU-SWAP COST IS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY, not overlooked: Synopsis routes to AiTaskType.Summarization -> qwen3.5:9b while Ai:FeatureModels:TermRepair is gemma4:12b, so on an OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 host every LEAKING synopsis costs a cross-model load (~21.5-34.3s, asymmetric, docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md section 19.2) plus a load back on the next Summarization-family call. It is bounded to GENUINE leaks - a clean synopsis makes ZERO model calls and q2 measured 0/6 legitimate values reaching the model - and Synopsis is produced ONCE per profile build, not once per chapter, on a path (BuildBookProfileAsync) that already interleaves qwen3.5:9b and gemma4:12b generation with zero repair involvement. That is the same trade s4 already ACCEPTED (docs section 19.4). RESIDUAL RISK, stated so it is not forgotten: rule (7b) spares a LINE-HEAD proper noun only (be-c03 restated it as a LINE head - ONE hard line break is enough, a blank line is NOT required, which is what the real persisted Synopsis / SummaryText prose actually uses); an external proper noun at a MID-LINE sentence head still reaches the repair model, and a synopsis is the value shape most likely to name one. VALUE-SCOPED LLM CARVE-OUT (be-c01, 2026-07-28): this key wires Synopsis into the two DETERMINISTIC dispatch switches only. It is DELIBERATELY not an arm in the third, AnalysisRepairService.RepairAnalysisAsync, so setting GuardOnly=false adds nothing for Synopsis - that stage never consults ForeignRunClassifier, so rule (7b) cannot protect it, and the only measurement of a repair model rewriting Synopsis prose is q1's 83%/1-FP HALT. The argument and its reversal condition are stated at that switch's default arm; see docs/ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_REPAIR.md sections 4.1 / 4.2. KILL-SWITCH: set this key back to false in BOTH files (the dispatch arms may stay - the gate closes ahead of them). See the plan's '## q2 quality-gate results' and '## f2 outcome', and docs sections 4.1 / 4.2. Proofread stays ABSENT rather than explicit-false: its exclusion is architectural (output quotes verbatim manuscript spans; repairing them would corrupt the suggestion diff), already stated independently in docs section 4 and inside all three dispatch switches' own default/fallback arms, and PerType is a map of things that MAY be flipped on - an explicit false here could misleadingly suggest Proofread is a config-level toggle, when enabling it would require rewriting the dispatch switches and would violate the verbatim-manuscript-span design rule. AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.EveryAnalysisType_HasAnExplicitRepairCoverageDecision (h2) accepts absent OR present-and-false for an excluded type, so this asymmetry between Custom and Proofread is a deliberate choice, not an inconsistency. KEEP THIS IN SYNC with the sibling appsettings file's own _comment_PerTypeExclusions (byte-identical) - AnalysisRepairConfigParityTests.PerType_BaseAndProduction_AreEqual only compares the boolean PerType values, not this comment, but drift here would make the two files' documented rationale disagree.
